key_insight: On the tested equity data, QCML behaved like a classical smoothing kernel, with no return-ranking gains from complex phases, noncommutativity, or circuit entanglement.
engineering_relevance: Capacity-matched classical baselines and norm-controlled spectral tests can help engineers determine whether quantum-inspired components add value beyond regularization and scale effects.
method: Progressively remove complex phases and noncommutativity using capacity-matched operator swaps.
Compare spectral crisis indicators against radial-norm nulls and untrained random matrices.
Evaluate variational circuits and classical controls under realistic trading constraints.
evidence_signal: Out-of-sample tests on Moscow Exchange equities from 2020–2025 with causally lagged macro news found no quantum-component ranking advantage, while feature normalization pushed spectral-gap crisis detection below chance.
watch_item: Findings are specific to the tested market and period, and reported economic benefits did not pass multiple-testing thresholds.
paper_title: Empirical De-Quantization and Norm-Controlled Spectral Audit of Quantum Cognition Machine Learning in an Emerging Equity Market
